title: Applying Game-Theoretic Adversarial Robustness Concepts to Multi-Agent Safety

original_idea.body:
# Applying Game-Theoretic Adversarial Robustness Concepts to Multi-Agent Safety

**Problem:** Game theory studies strategic interactions between self-interested agents. Its adversarial robustness concepts (e.g., Nash equilibria in adversarial games) have not been applied to multi-agent AI safety scenarios where agents may develop adversarial strategies.

**Direction:** Model a two-agent scenario (task-completion agent + safety monitor agent) as a Stackelberg game. Compute theoretical Nash equilibria where the task agent maximizes task completion and the monitor maximizes detection. Test whether empirical agent behavior in simulation matches the theoretical equilibrium predictions.

**Why it matters:** Game-theoretic analysis can predict whether safety monitoring arms races are stable or lead to an equilibrium where safety is undermined. This provides theoretical grounding for multi-agent safety design.

**Relevant context:** Stackelberg games; mechanism design; Irregular 2026 inter-agent collusion; multi-agent RL security.
